name: sg-glower
summary: Full-bleed hero running shader.gallery's glower: storm towers at night over a dark plain, with slow violet and white glows swelling and wandering inside the billows, never flashing. A town on the plain burns the cloud bases sodium orange, rain hangs under the far cells and a flooded field mirrors the glow.

colors.description: Four storm tones. 1 is the strongest glow inside the clouds, 2 the pale ones; 0 tints the cloud crowns and the flood; 3 is the deep sky. Omit to read --fx-c1 through --fx-c4 off the section, which is what keeps the shader and the CSS resting state on one palette.

glow.description: How strongly the glows inside the clouds light the billows around them. Upstream default, range 0.2 to 2.

churn.description: How fast the towers boil and the glows wander and swell. Upstream default, range 0 to 2.5.

town.description: Warm sodium light of the town on the plain and on the cloud bases. Upstream default, range 0 to 2.

deviations.what: The four u_palette colours are ours, not upstream's `umbra` preset.
deviations.why: glower/meta.json declares `defaultPalette: "umbra"`, and the preset table lives in @shader-gallery/runtime, a package paw-fx does not vendor and which is not in the pinned repo. The port cannot resolve the name, so it ships four of its own, picked off the upstream poster by eye, and declares them. Same call sg-obsidian, sg-gloam and sg-bask made.

deviations.what: No post chain: upstream's poster runs grain 0.04, vignette 0.3, bloom 0.4 (radius 4) and dither over the shader output.
deviations.why: The post chain lives in @shader-gallery/runtime, a package paw-fx does not vendor. Our output is the raw shader, so it will not match the upstream poster. The glows inside the clouds and the town lights lean on that bloom, so the live hero reads a little harder-edged than the poster. The section's own CSS grain layer stands in for the poster grain.

deviations.what: Rendered through paw-fx's own WebGL runtime (effects/_shared/glsl-mount.js) rather than @shader-gallery/runtime.
deviations.why: Seam. Upstream ships the .frag with no module around it. The GLSL itself is byte-identical to upstream and lives in shader.frag beside index.js.
